messages:
lara: Quick update — ran a regional econ sweep comparing A100 vs H100 for two common 7B configs (llama-2-7b q4_0, mosaic-7b q8_0). Short summary below, full logs in the gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/bench-1805 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

bench-bot: Auto-summary: 4 regions, 2 models, 2 quant configs, kernels: triton-attn-v3 vs aten. 7200 sample runs per config.

santiago: Nice. Can you paste the prefill/decode medians and tokens/sec so I can size capacity?

lara: Pasting the median numbers we care about (prefill = first forward to build KV, decode = per-token tail latency). These are p50 medians across the run (no heavy tail trimming). Costs estimated using commit pricing + infra $/hour we use for econ math.

lara: ```
Model (quant)    GPU   region    prefill_ms   decode_ms_per_token   tok_per_s   $/1M_tokens
llama-2-7b (q4_0) H100  us-west   95           3.9                   256         $0.64
llama-2-7b (q4_0) A100  us-west   140          6.5                   154         $1.05
llama-2-7b (q4_0) H100  eu-west   105          4.2                   238         $0.69
llama-2-7b (q4_0) A100  eu-west   155          7.2                   138         $1.12

mosaic-7b (q8_0) H100  us-west   110          4.5                   222         $0.74
mosaic-7b (q8_0) A100  us-west   160          7.1                   141         $1.15
```

anya: Pretty clear H100 wins on decode throughput and $/1M tokens. Any kernel diffs?

lara: Yes — kernel sweep: `triton-attn-v3` vs `aten` default. Triton gave ~10-12% decode improvement on H100 for both models (lower decode_ms/token), and a couple ms lower prefill in some runs. On A100 the delta was smaller (4-6%). Also tested KV cache prefetching (helped high-batch workloads).

zach: What about quantization quality tradeoffs? We need to know ROUGE/EM regressions for q4_0 vs q8_0.

lara: Short: q4_0 on llama-2-7b showed ~1.8% drop on our chat-turn eval (avg), q8_0 negligible (<0.5%). For mosaics q8_0 is baseline. So cost vs quality: H100+q4_0 is cheapest but slightly more quality risk.

bench-bot: Note: We observed region noise ~+8-12% latency in eu compared to us-west for same instance types, likely due to instance SKU differences (smaller PCIe NVLink on eu nodes).

lara: Capacity sizing note — rule of thumb with our batching profile (avg request 30 tokens, batching latency SLO 200ms):
- To sustain 100k tokens/s steady for llama-2-7b(q4_0): ~390 A100s or ~155 H100s (based on tok_per_s above and util headroom).
- For mosaic-7b(q8_0): ~475 A100s or ~215 H100s.
(These are quick extrapolations — use per-route profiling before commit).

santiago: Cool. Any ops flags we should toggle in Dedicated to save cost?

lara: Yes — enable KV prefix caching for hot routes, set small decode batch limits for low-latency routes, prefer `triton-attn-v3` on H100. Also consider serving llama-2-7b(q4_0) from eu for EU customers only if quality drop acceptable, else route to us-west H100 for the higher Q/SLA tier.

anya: Thx. Can you attach the raw CSV and the kernel configs in the gist? I'll add to the perf-runbook.

lara: Done — gist has raw CSV, command lines, and the `triton` kernel args we used. TL;DR: H100 wins across decode throughput and $/1M tokens; regional SKU differences matter; kernel choice amplifies H100 advantage.

zach: Great, will add notes to the `model-onboarding` checklist and recommend default H100 + triton for new 7B bring-ups unless customer's cost sensitivity forces A100 + q8_0. :thumbsup:
